html:
On 14 July 1958 army officers led by Abd al-Karim Qasim overthrew the monarchy of Iraq. The young King Faisal II and much of the royal family were shot in the palace in Baghdad, and the pro-British prime minister Nuri al-Said was killed the next day.

The officers were inspired by Nasser's revolution in Egypt and angered by the monarchy's ties to Britain. Qasim made Iraq a republic, gave land to peasants and left the Western Baghdad Pact. He clashed with Arab nationalists who wanted to join the United Arab Republic.

Qasim was overthrown and killed in 1963 by the Ba'ath Party, which took power for good in 1968. That opened the way for Saddam Hussein. The day is a national holiday in Iraq.
